The setup required no rearrangement or search of any kind. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage, due to exemplary cockpit organization of charts and plates.

error_modes.label: CHECKLIST INTERRUPTION RECOVERY AND (BOTH) CHALLENGE AND RESPONSE

texts.0: SP, due to an interruption during the flow and a failure to restart the checklist at the prescribed point, did not positively confirm completion of the checklist after the break. SP resumed several steps beyond the interrupted item, gave lip service to a standardized phrase without performing the check behind it and treated a (BOTH) item as complete with no response from the rear cockpit. The IP intervened, stopped the flow and had the checklist re-run from the top before the next checklist was started.
texts.1: SP, due to an interruption on the intercom during the flow, did not restart at the first step of the checklist nor two to three steps prior to the interrupted step. SP resumed from memory at the wrong point and needed three verbal indications from the IP to identify the omitted item and to obtain the proper response to the (BOTH) challenge. The checklist was finally confirmed complete, but the recovery was entirely directed by the IP.
texts.2: SP, due to a radio call cutting into the flow, did not resume the checklist at the correct recovery point and initially picked up beyond the interrupted step. SP recognized the break in the sequence, went back two to three steps prior to the interrupted item and reissued the (BOTH) challenge until a proper response was received. The checklist was positively confirmed complete before the next one was started, with no IP intervention.
texts.3: SP handled the interruption by restarting the checklist two to three steps prior to the interrupted step and positively confirmed completion of every item before starting the next checklist. SP challenged each (BOTH) item and treated it as complete only after a proper response from the other cockpit. No item was omitted and no IP input was required.
texts.4: SP protected the checklist flow from interruptions, deferred the intercom exchange to a break point and, where an interruption was unavoidable, resumed exactly two to three steps prior to the interrupted item. SP verified every item against the printed page after completing the flow and obtained a proper response to each (BOTH) challenge without prompting. No omission, no repetition and no IP involvement of any kind occurred.
texts.marginal: SP recovered from the interruption at an acceptable point and positively confirmed completion of the checklist, so the standard was met. However SP allowed the intercom exchange to cut into the flow rather than holding it to a break point, and issued the (BOTH) challenge a second time only after the IP paused, which shows the discipline is not yet consolidated. SP is expected to protect the flow from avoidable interruptions and to hold each (BOTH) item open until the response is received.

texts_at.0: With the IP naming the point to resume after the interruption and prompting the (BOTH) challenge again, SP restarted the checklist from the point given. The rule of resuming two to three steps prior to an interruption has not yet been learned, so the resume point is still supplied rather than judged independently. The Training Section introduces this maneuver at this point and does not yet ask for an independent standard. SP is expected to begin resuming two to three steps prior to the interruption without the point being named.
texts_at.1: SP identified the omitted item and obtained the proper response to the (BOTH) challenge only after three verbal indications from the IP, because the checklist had been resumed from memory at the wrong point after an intercom interruption. The checklist was confirmed complete once the indications had been given. Performance met the desired standard for this stage. SP is expected to resume two to three steps prior to the interrupted item without needing the location pointed out.
texts_at.2: SP recognized a break in the sequence caused by a radio call, went back two to three steps prior to the interrupted item and reissued the (BOTH) challenge until a proper response was received, with no IP intervention. The checklist was positively confirmed complete before the next one was started. This is consistent with the expected proficiency for the Training Section. SP is expected to protect the flow from the radio call in the first place so no recovery step is needed.
texts_at.3: SP restarted the checklist two to three steps prior to the interrupted step and positively confirmed completion of every item before starting the next checklist, challenging each (BOTH) item and treating it as complete only after a proper response. The intercom exchange was allowed to cut into the flow rather than being held to a break point. The standard for the Training Section was met. SP is expected to defer the intercom exchange to a break point on the next sortie.

texts_above.1: SP identified the omitted checklist item and obtained the proper (BOTH) response. The correction followed three verbal indications from the IP. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus.
texts_above.2: SP resumed the checklist two to three steps prior to an intercom interruption and reissued the (BOTH) challenge until a proper response was received, with no item omitted and no IP intervention needed. The checklist was positively confirmed complete before the next one began. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to steady checklist interruption recovery.
texts_above.3: SP protected the checklist flow from the intercom exchange on most of the sortie and, on the one occasion an interruption could not be avoided, resumed exactly two to three steps prior to the interrupted item and verified every item against the printed page. No (BOTH) challenge needed a second issue. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus, due to consistently accurate checklist interruption recovery.
texts_above.4: SP deferred every intercom exchange to a break point in the flow, so no checklist interruption occurred across the whole sortie and every (BOTH) challenge received a proper response without prompting. No omission, repetition or IP involvement of any kind occurred. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage, due to exceptional checklist interruption recovery.

error_modes.label: USE OF UNCONGESTED TAXI TIME FOR DEPARTURE AND NAVAID PREPARATION

texts.0: SP, due to not using uncongested taxi time to prepare for takeoff and departure, did not review the weather, the winds, the departure routing, the NAVAID setup and the takeoff emergencies before reaching the holding point. SP arrived at the runway with the navigation aids untuned for the assigned departure and with no review of the takeoff emergency actions. The IP intervened, held the aircraft at the holding point and had the whole preparation completed there before line up was requested.
texts.1: SP, due to leaving the departure preparation until the holding point instead of using the uncongested taxi segments, did not complete the NAVAID setup and the takeoff emergency review in time. SP worked through the items only after three verbal indications from the IP naming each element of the acronym in turn. The preparation was completed before line up, but entirely under IP direction.
texts.2: SP, due to concentrating on the taxi path during the uncongested segment, did not begin the departure preparation until after the first turn out of parking. SP recognized the delay, used the remaining straight segment to tune and identify the departure aids, confirm the routing and review the takeoff emergencies. All items were covered before the holding point with no IP intervention.
texts.3: SP used the uncongested taxi segments to prepare for takeoff and departure, covering weather, winds, departure routing, NAVAID setup and takeoff emergencies in the order given by the SOP acronym. SP kept the taxi path and the clearing scan unaffected while working the items. The preparation was complete before the holding point without IP input.
texts.4: SP distributed the departure preparation across the uncongested taxi segments so that every item of the SOP acronym was covered well before the holding point, with each departure aid tuned and identified. SP interrupted the preparation cleanly at every turn and congested area and resumed it afterwards, with no effect on taxi path or clearing. Nothing remained to be done at the holding point and no IP involvement of any kind was required.
texts.marginal: SP covered weather, winds, routing, NAVAID setup and takeoff emergencies before the holding point, so the standard was met. However SP worked two of the items while approaching a turn instead of reserving them for the uncongested straight segment, and the last aid was identified only as the aircraft stopped at the holding point. SP is expected to front-load the preparation into the uncongested segments and to suspend it whenever the taxi situation demands full attention.

texts_at.0: With the IP naming each element of the departure-preparation acronym in turn, SP worked through the items named during the uncongested taxi segments. The SOP acronym for departure preparation has not yet been learned well enough to work through independently, so each element is still supplied rather than recalled. This is the level of assistance the Training Section still provides at this stage. SP is expected to begin working through the acronym from memory without each element being named.
texts_at.1: SP completed the NAVAID setup and the takeoff emergency review only after three verbal indications from the IP naming each element of the acronym, because the departure preparation had been left until the holding point instead of using the uncongested taxi segments. The preparation was complete before line up once the indications had been given. Performance met the desired standard for this stage. SP is expected to start the preparation on the uncongested segments without needing each element prompted.
texts_at.2: SP recognized that the departure preparation had not begun until after the first turn out of parking, then used the remaining straight segment to tune and identify the departure aids, confirm the routing and review the takeoff emergencies, with no IP intervention. All items were covered before the holding point. This is consistent with the expected proficiency for the Training Section. SP is expected to begin the preparation from the first uncongested segment rather than the second.
texts_at.3: SP used the uncongested taxi segments to prepare for takeoff and departure, covering weather, winds, departure routing, NAVAID setup and takeoff emergencies in the order given by the SOP acronym, without affecting the taxi path or the clearing scan. Two of the items were worked while approaching a turn rather than on the preceding straight segment. The standard for the Training Section was met. SP is expected to reserve the turns for taxiing alone and finish the items beforehand.

texts_above.1: SP completed the NAVAID setup and the takeoff emergency review before line up. The correction followed three verbal indications from the IP, one for each element of the acronym. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage of training.
texts_above.2: SP covered weather, winds, departure routing, NAVAID setup and takeoff emergencies across the uncongested taxi segments, working two items while approaching a turn but completing them before it began, without any IP input. The taxi path and the clearing scan were unaffected throughout. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to dependable use of uncongested taxi time.
texts_above.3: SP covered every item of the SOP acronym in the uncongested straight segments and kept the taxi path and clearing scan unaffected while doing so, with the preparation complete well before the holding point. No item was left for the holding point itself. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus, due to notably good use of uncongested taxi time.
texts_above.4: SP distributed every item of the SOP acronym across the uncongested taxi segments so nothing remained to be done at the holding point, interrupting the preparation cleanly at every turn and congested area and resuming it afterward with no effect on taxi path or clearing. No IP involvement of any kind was required. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage, due to superior use of uncongested taxi time.

error_modes.label: BEFORE TAKEOFF CHECKS, LINE UP CHAIN OF ACTIONS AND TOLD REVIEW
error_modes.source: technique:3.11 BEFORE TAKEOFF AND LINEUP CHECKS

texts.0: SP, due to following a personal habit instead of the prescribed chain of Before Takeoff Checks, request line up and line up, inserted other checks and procedures between the Before Takeoff Checks and line up. SP also accepted the briefed TOLD unchanged although the reported conditions differed significantly from the forecast, so the takeoff data used no longer matched the actual wind and temperature. The IP intervened, stopped the line up request and had the TOLD recomputed and the Before Takeoff Checks re-run immediately before line up.
texts.1: SP, due to a habitual sequence that placed avionics work after the Before Takeoff Checks, did not execute those checks last, right before line up. SP started the TOLD review only after three verbal indications from the IP that the reported conditions differed significantly from the forecast. The chain was eventually flown in the correct order and the TOLD was recomputed, but every step required IP direction.
texts.2: SP, due to treating the Before Takeoff Checks as just another checklist in the flow, began an unrelated avionics setup after completing them. SP recognized the break in the chain before transmitting, finished the avionics item, re-ran the Before Takeoff Checks and only then requested line up. The TOLD was reviewed against the reported conditions and no IP intervention was required.
texts.3: SP reviewed the TOLD against the reported conditions and executed the Before Takeoff Checks last, with no other checks or procedures between them and line up. SP followed the chain of Before Takeoff Checks, request line up and line up in that order. The sequence was completed correctly without IP input.
texts.4: SP recomputed the TOLD with the actual reported conditions as soon as they were passed, then held the Before Takeoff Checks until everything else was finished so that they were the last action before the line up request. SP flew the chain of Before Takeoff Checks, request line up and line up with nothing inserted between them and stated the recomputed abort speed and distance before rolling. No repetition and no IP involvement of any kind were required.
texts.marginal: SP reviewed the TOLD and executed the Before Takeoff Checks immediately before line up with nothing inserted in between, so the standard was met. However SP began the TOLD comparison only after the IP asked whether the reported wind matched the forecast, and completed the checks with the aircraft already rolling toward the holding point. SP is expected to trigger the TOLD comparison on the reported conditions themselves and to complete the Before Takeoff Checks stopped, immediately before requesting line up.

texts_at.0: With the IP calling out that the reported conditions differed from the forecast and naming the correct sequence, SP reviewed the TOLD and flew the chain on the calls given. The chain of Before Takeoff Checks, request line up and line up has not yet settled into a fixed habit, so the sequence is still supplied rather than followed from memory. The maneuver is being introduced at this point of the syllabus, so no independent standard is required yet. SP is expected to begin comparing the reported conditions to the forecast without the difference being called.
texts_at.1: SP began the TOLD comparison only after three verbal indications from the IP that the reported conditions differed significantly from the forecast, because a habitual sequence had placed avionics work after the Before Takeoff Checks. The chain was eventually flown in the correct order once the indications had been given. Performance met the desired standard for this stage. SP is expected to trigger the TOLD comparison on the reported conditions themselves rather than on a prompt.
texts_at.2: SP recognized a break in the chain caused by an unrelated avionics setup after the Before Takeoff Checks, finished the avionics item, re-ran the checks and only then requested line up, with no IP intervention. The TOLD was reviewed against the reported conditions before the request. This is consistent with the expected proficiency for the Training Section. SP is expected to complete the avionics setup before starting the Before Takeoff Checks so the break does not occur.
texts_at.3: SP reviewed the TOLD against the reported conditions and executed the Before Takeoff Checks last, with nothing inserted between them and the line up request, following the chain of checks, request and line up in order. The TOLD comparison began only once the IP asked whether the reported wind matched the forecast. The standard for the Training Section was met. SP is expected to trigger the comparison on the reported conditions themselves on the next sortie.

texts_above.1: SP flew the Before Takeoff Checks, request line up and line up chain in the correct order, recomputing the TOLD for the changed conditions. The correction followed three verbal indications from the IP. This is above the level the Training Section requires at this point.
texts_above.2: SP reviewed the TOLD against the reported conditions and executed the Before Takeoff Checks last, with one avionics item finished before the checks began rather than after, and required no IP input to keep the chain in order. Line up was requested only once the sequence was complete. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to assured handling of the before-takeoff chain of actions.
texts_above.3: SP recomputed the TOLD against the reported conditions and flew the chain of Before Takeoff Checks, request line up and line up with nothing inserted between them on every occasion. The sequence held even when the reported wind and temperature differed from the forecast. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus, due to precise handling of the before-takeoff chain of actions.
texts_above.4: SP recomputed the TOLD with the actual reported conditions as soon as they were passed and held the Before Takeoff Checks until everything else was finished, stating the recomputed abort speed and distance before rolling. No repetition or IP involvement of any kind was required. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage, due to exceptional handling of the before-takeoff chain of actions.

error_modes.label: OVER SPEED GOVERNOR CHECK CLEARING, POWER APPLICATION AND BRAKE GUARDING

texts.0: SP, due to remaining head down on the instruments instead of clearing outside the aircraft, did not ensure that the area immediately in front of and behind the aircraft was clear before the over speed governor check. SP advanced the power abruptly and higher than required to verify proper function, with the control stick forward, and the aircraft crept forward on compressed nose gear. The IP intervened, took the power lever and the brakes and stopped the check before it was completed.
texts.1: SP, due to an incomplete outside scan before the run up, did not confirm that the area behind the aircraft was clear and did not announce the check to the other cockpit. SP advanced the power in one coarse movement and needed three verbal indications from the IP to reduce it, to hold the stick neutral to slightly aft and to clear outside during the check. The check was completed correctly, but only under IP direction.
texts.2: SP, due to concentrating on the engine indications, did not clear outside the aircraft at the start of the power advance and let the control stick go slightly forward. SP recognized the omission, brought the stick back to the neutral to slightly aft position and resumed the outside scan while advancing the power smoothly to the value required. The check was verified correctly with no IP intervention.
texts.3: SP ensured the area immediately in front of and behind the aircraft was clear, advanced the power smoothly and slowly only as high as required to verify proper function of the over speed governor, and cleared outside the aircraft during the check. SP kept the control stick neutral to slightly aft so the nose gear strut did not compress, and the aircraft stayed stationary. The check was completed without IP input.
texts.4: SP cleared the area in front of and behind the aircraft, announced the check, then advanced the power smoothly and slowly to exactly the setting required to verify proper function of the over speed governor. SP held the control stick neutral to slightly aft, kept a continuous outside scan through the whole run up and confirmed that the pilot not flying was guarding the brakes. The aircraft did not move, no repetition was needed and no IP involvement of any kind occurred.
texts.marginal: SP cleared the area, advanced the power smoothly and verified the over speed governor with the aircraft stationary, so the standard was met. However SP carried the power slightly higher than needed to obtain the indication and let the outside scan lapse for a moment while reading the gauges, which shows the division of attention is not yet settled. SP is expected to stop the power advance at the minimum setting that verifies proper function and to keep clearing outside throughout the check.

texts_at.0: With the IP naming each step of the check in turn, including the outside scan, the power application and the stick position, SP performed the steps named. The sequence of the over speed governor check has not yet been learned as a single flow, so each step is still supplied rather than recalled in order. Performance is consistent with a first exposure at this point of the syllabus, where the Training Section still provides assistance. SP is expected to begin flying the outside scan before the run up without it being named.
texts_at.1: SP reduced the power, held the stick neutral to slightly aft and cleared outside during the over speed governor check only after three verbal indications from the IP, because the outside scan before the run up had been incomplete. The check was completed correctly once the indications had been given. Performance met the desired standard for this stage. SP is expected to complete the outside scan before the run up without needing each step named.
texts_at.2: SP recognized that the control stick had gone slightly forward and the outside scan had lapsed while attention was on the engine indications, brought the stick back to neutral to slightly aft and resumed the scan while advancing power smoothly, with no IP intervention. The check was verified correctly. This is consistent with the expected proficiency for the Training Section. SP is expected to hold the stick position and the outside scan together from the start of the check.
texts_at.3: SP ensured the area was clear, advanced the power smoothly and slowly only as high as required to verify proper function, and cleared outside during the check while keeping the control stick neutral to slightly aft. The power was carried a touch higher than needed to obtain the indication on one occasion. The standard for the Training Section was met. SP is expected to stop the power advance at the minimum setting that verifies proper function.

texts_above.1: SP completed the over speed governor check correctly, reducing power, holding the stick and clearing outside. The correction followed three verbal indications from the IP. The result is above the code required for this Training Section at this stage of training.
texts_above.2: SP cleared the area and advanced the power smoothly, holding the control stick close to neutral to slightly aft, and caught one moment where the outside scan lapsed while reading the gauges, resuming it without any IP input. The aircraft stayed stationary throughout the check. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to competent over speed governor check technique.
texts_above.3: SP cleared the area, advanced the power smoothly and slowly to exactly the setting required and kept a continuous outside scan through the whole run up, with the control stick held neutral to slightly aft throughout. The aircraft did not move at any point in the check. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus, due to disciplined over speed governor check technique.
texts_above.4: SP announced the check, advanced the power smoothly to exactly the setting required and confirmed the pilot not flying was guarding the brakes, with a continuous outside scan through the whole run up and no movement of the aircraft. No repetition or IP involvement of any kind occurred. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage, due to faultless over speed governor check technique.

error_modes.label: READ BACK OF ATC CLEARANCE AND TAXI INSTRUCTIONS

texts.0: SP, due to not listening carefully to the taxi instructions and treating the read back as optional, did not read back the ATC clearance, which is always required because it ensures understanding. SP acknowledged an instruction that contained a hold short element without repeating it and started to move toward the wrong taxiway. The IP intervened, stopped the aircraft, transmitted the correct read back and had the instruction confirmed before taxi continued.
texts.1: SP, due to not listening carefully to the taxi instructions, did not read back the routing and omitted the hold short element from the acknowledgement. SP produced a complete and correct read back only after three verbal indications from the IP and one request for repetition to the controller. The instruction was finally understood, but the whole exchange was carried by the IP.
texts.2: SP, due to writing while the controller was still transmitting, did not capture the full taxi routing and read back only the first two elements. SP recognized the gap immediately, requested one repetition on own initiative and transmitted a complete read back including the hold short instruction before releasing the brakes. No IP intervention was required.
texts.3: SP listened carefully to the taxi instructions and read back the ATC clearance completely and correctly, including the hold short element. SP also read back an instruction that differed from the standard routing to confirm understanding before acting on it. The whole radio exchange was handled without IP input.
texts.4: SP read back every clearance and taxi instruction completely and correctly at the first attempt, with standard phraseology and no request for repetition. SP identified an instruction that differed from the standard routing, read it back specifically to confirm understanding and stated the intended path to the other cockpit before moving. No correction and no IP involvement of any kind were required.
texts.marginal: SP read back the ATC clearance and the taxi instructions completely, including the hold short element, so the standard was met. However SP began the read back before the controller had finished and had to append the last element after a pause, and did not query an instruction that differed from the standard routing until the IP mentioned it. SP is expected to let the transmission finish before answering and to read back on own initiative anything that appears different than standard.

texts_at.0: With the IP naming the missing elements of the taxi instructions and prompting the read back, SP repeated the instructions element by element as named. The habit of capturing every element of a clearance on the first transmission has not yet been built, so missing elements are still identified by the IP rather than by SP. The Training Section still expects IP assistance for this maneuver at this point. SP is expected to begin capturing every element from the controller's first transmission without the missing ones being named.
texts_at.1: SP produced a complete and correct read back of the taxi instructions only after three verbal indications from the IP and one request for repetition to the controller, because the instructions had not been listened to carefully enough to capture every element. The instruction was understood correctly once the read back was complete. Performance met the desired standard for this stage. SP is expected to capture every element from the controller's first transmission.
texts_at.2: SP recognized that only the first two elements of the taxi routing had been captured while writing during the transmission, requested one repetition on own initiative and transmitted a complete read back including the hold short instruction, with no IP intervention. The brakes were not released until the read back was complete. This is consistent with the expected proficiency for the Training Section. SP is expected to finish writing after the transmission ends rather than during it.
texts_at.3: SP listened carefully to the taxi instructions and read back the ATC clearance completely and correctly, including the hold short element, and also read back an instruction that differed from the standard routing to confirm understanding. The read back began before the controller had quite finished, with the last element appended after a short pause. The standard for the Training Section was met. SP is expected to let the transmission finish before beginning the read back.

texts_above.1: SP produced a complete and correct read back of the taxi instructions, needing one request for repetition to the controller. The correction followed three verbal indications from the IP. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus.
texts_above.2: SP read back the ATC clearance and taxi instructions completely, including the hold short element, catching one instruction that differed from the standard routing and reading it back to confirm understanding without any IP input. The whole radio exchange was handled without a request for repetition. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to steady radio read-back discipline.
texts_above.3: SP read back every clearance and taxi instruction completely and correctly on the first attempt, including the hold short element, and identified an instruction that differed from the standard routing before acting on it. The whole exchange was handled with standard phraseology throughout. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus, due to sure-handed radio read-back discipline.
texts_above.4: SP read back every clearance and taxi instruction completely and correctly at the first attempt with standard phraseology, identified an instruction that differed from the standard routing and stated the intended path to the other cockpit before moving. No correction or IP involvement of any kind was required. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage, due to outstanding radio read-back discipline.

error_modes.label: AFTER LANDING CLEARANCE, SHUTDOWN VIGILANCE AND OVER THE RAIL CHECK

texts.0: SP, due to complacency after landing and treating the sortie as complete at touchdown, did not obtain clearance before crossing the active runway on the way back to the ramp. During shutdown SP lost sight of the ground personnel and left the aircraft without the over the rail check, so the ejection pin and CFS pin state was never confirmed. The IP intervened, stopped the aircraft short of the runway, obtained the clearance and had the shutdown items completed before the aircraft was left.
texts.1: SP, due to complacency after landing, did not request clearance before proceeding back to the ramp and did not keep the ground personnel in sight during shutdown. SP completed the after landing and shutdown items only after three verbal indications from the IP, including the reminder to do the over the rail check before stepping down from the wing. Everything was eventually completed, but under continuous IP direction.
texts.2: SP, due to relaxing attention after clearing the runway, did not request the crossing clearance at the first opportunity and stopped short only when the holding position was reached. SP recognized the omission, obtained the clearance before crossing, kept the ground personnel in sight during shutdown and did the over the rail check before stepping down. No IP intervention was required.
texts.3: SP obtained clearance before crossing the active runway and before proceeding back to the ramp, taxied with caution and stayed alert until the aircraft was parked. SP kept the ground personnel in sight during shutdown and did the over the rail check, confirming ejection pin and CFS pin in, ISS in SOLO, battery switch off, OBOGS lever off and parking brake as required. All items were completed without IP input.
texts.4: SP requested each clearance before crossing the active runway and before proceeding to the ramp without prompting, and maintained the same attention level as before takeoff until the engine was shut down. SP kept the ground personnel in sight throughout, was ready to shut down immediately if the propeller safety zone was violated, and completed the over the rail check item by item before stepping down from the wing. The post flight walk around followed and no IP involvement of any kind was required.
texts.marginal: SP obtained the required clearances, kept the ground personnel in sight and completed the over the rail check before stepping down, so the standard was met. However SP called for the crossing clearance late enough to require a stop at the holding position, and ran the over the rail items as a quick sweep rather than confirming each one, which shows attention is already dropping before the sortie is complete. SP is expected to request the clearance early enough to keep the aircraft rolling and to confirm each over the rail item individually.

texts_at.0: With the IP naming each after-landing and shutdown item in turn, including the over the rail check, SP completed the items named. The after-landing and shutdown sequence has not yet been learned as a single flow, so each item is still supplied rather than recalled from memory. The Training Section introduces this maneuver at this point and does not yet ask for an independent standard. SP is expected to begin recalling the shutdown sequence, including the over the rail check, without each item being named.
texts_at.1: SP completed the after landing and shutdown items, including the over the rail check, only after three verbal indications from the IP, because attention had relaxed once the sortie reached touchdown. Every item was completed correctly once the indications had been given. Performance met the desired standard for this stage. SP is expected to carry the same attention level through shutdown without needing each item named.
texts_at.2: SP recognized that the crossing clearance had not been requested at the first opportunity, obtained it before crossing, kept the ground personnel in sight during shutdown and did the over the rail check before stepping down, with no IP intervention. No item was left unconfirmed. This is consistent with the expected proficiency for the Training Section. SP is expected to request the crossing clearance at the first opportunity rather than after the holding position is reached.
texts_at.3: SP obtained clearance before crossing the active runway and before proceeding back to the ramp, kept the ground personnel in sight during shutdown and did the over the rail check, confirming ejection pin, CFS pin, ISS, battery switch, OBOGS lever and parking brake as required. The crossing clearance was requested late enough to need a stop at the holding position. The standard for the Training Section was met. SP is expected to request the clearance early enough to keep the aircraft rolling.

texts_above.1: SP completed the after landing and shutdown items, including the over the rail check. The correction followed three verbal indications from the IP. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage of training.
texts_above.2: SP obtained the required clearances, kept the ground personnel in sight through shutdown and completed the over the rail check before stepping down, catching one late crossing-clearance call and requesting it before the holding position was reached without any IP input. Every over the rail item was confirmed individually. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to good after-landing and shutdown vigilance.
texts_above.3: SP requested each clearance before crossing the active runway and before proceeding to the ramp, kept the ground personnel in sight throughout and completed the over the rail check item by item before stepping down from the wing. The same attention level carried from before takeoff to engine shutdown. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus, due to consistently accurate after-landing and shutdown vigilance.
texts_above.4: SP requested every clearance without prompting, stayed ready to shut down immediately if the propeller safety zone was violated and completed the over the rail check item by item before stepping down, with the post flight walk around following directly. No IP involvement of any kind was required at any stage. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage, due to exemplary after-landing and shutdown vigilance.
